title: [DTensor] Reject random ops on mismatched local tensor and mesh devices
body:
A CPU-local DTensor on an accelerator mesh enters the accelerator RNG tracker, which restores CPU RNG state and can repeatedly generate the same samples. Reject mismatched non-meta local devices before constructing the tracker or executing the random operation. Preserve meta initialization and matching-device behavior.

Add regressions for random operators, placements, tracker initialization, input and RNG preservation, and the FSDP meta-to-CPU initialization path. This follows the error-on-mismatch approach proposed in closed PR #180087 and fixes #180088.

Test Plan
=========
On the remote RTX 3090 host:
```bash
bash /ch_data/wzp/oss-ai-infra/pytorch-dtensor-rng-device-20260919/run_gpu.sh fixed-verified test/distributed/tensor/test_random_ops.py -k device_mismatch -v

cd /ch_data/wzp/oss-ai-infra/pytorch-dtensor-rng-device-20260919/repo
env -u PYTHONPATH CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 ../.venv/bin/python test/distributed/tensor/test_random_ops.py DistTensorRandomInitTest.test_init_ops DistTensorRandomInitTestWithLocalTensor.test_init_ops -v

lintrunner -a
```
34 focused regressions and 2 CPU controls pass; 8 existing accelerator controls also pass. The added two-GPU regression fails on the unmodified source. Applicable lint checks pass. Validation used current-main Python source with existing CUDA 13.0 nightly native libraries, not a clean native build at this base. Full upstream CI and other accelerators were not run.
